prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B005 as a single part for Buchwald and Hartwig. Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general method whose mechanism (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination, with ligand design controlling each step) is understood, and it has been independently confirmed for about three decades and is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. The two independent ligand families give a credit boundary that is nearly as clean as any on the shortlist, and a two-person prize fits it. Round 1 sharpened my view of the contrast with B037: the four B037 supporters all concede that no PROTAC is approved and that every trio omits Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim, while B005 has no comparable clinical or allocation gap. I weigh a mature, unambiguous result above momentum.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize honoured Pd-catalysed C-C coupling, so a sceptic can read B005 as a second Pd-coupling award for a different bond. I think C-N coupling needed distinct ligand design and mechanism, but the objection is real. Kosugi's tin-amide work and Migita's precedent mean first discovery is not perfectly clean, and the two-name credit leaves them out. B037 is the more conceptually transformative idea for drug discovery and has the broadest opening support (four of eight explicit preferences in round 1), so the committee may judge B005 safe but less novel. Hartwig also appears on another candidate.

responses.point: Now regards Handa as the stronger third name for B037 because the cereblon glue mechanism is a separate and decisive discovery, and accepts that the PROTAC and glue strands could be two achievements.
responses.response: Your own reasoning is what keeps me from moving. If the cereblon mechanism is a separate and decisive discovery, then B037 is a design strand plus a mechanism strand, and the trio Crews, Deshaies, Handa stops being one achievement with obvious owners. Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim are dropped on a judgement that you yourself describe as unsettled. Your question of whether this is drug modality rather than chemistry also counts against it. I respect the ternary-complex and cooperativity science, but I do not see that the attribution question is resolved by the third name moving from Ciulli to Handa.

responses.point: Ranks B037 first but names B005 as the safer choice on maturity and attribution if the committee is early on degraders.
responses.response: We agree on the condition: if B037 is early, B005 is the right fallback. Where we differ is on whether it is early. Lenalidomide worked clinically before its mechanism was known, and with no approved bifunctional degrader the PROTAC half of the prize rests on promise rather than outcome. I would rather award the C-N coupling now, which is secure, than hope the pipeline validates the choice. On your 2010 question I answer that C-N coupling is a different bond-forming problem with its own ligand families and rate-limiting steps, so it is distinct.

responses.point: Chair and first-place B037 supporter; acknowledges that his ranking may reflect an appealing story more than a settled verdict and that B016 and B005 are more mature with cleaner credit.
responses.response: Your candour about the story outrunning the verdict is the point I find most persuasive. You name B016 and B005 as the options with cleaner credit and maturity, and B037 has four of the five votes needed. If the committee cannot settle the Sakamoto and Ciulli question or accept the clinical gap, B005 is the natural place to consolidate. I will not tell you B037 is poor science, but I do not think a prize of this standing should take the risk when the attribution is open.

responses.point: Proposes B016 for Car and Parrinello, acknowledging that DFT (1998) and multiscale modelling (2013) may count against another computational prize.
responses.response: I still regard B016 as a fully mature, cleanly credited achievement and would not object to it. Your own caveat about the 1998 and 2013 prizes and the question of how to cite Parrinello's later work are the reasons I rank it behind B005, together with the fact that only four members ranked it in the opening round. I have moved it into my alternatives, since it is the second candidate on the shortlist that reduces to a two-name credit with no allocation problem, and I would support it over B037 if the committee wants a computational prize.

responses.point: Prefers B005 and holds his ordering open pending whether B037 or B002 become cleaner on attribution.
responses.response: Round 1 did not make B037 cleaner: all four supporters still name the same trio with different citation wording and concede the same omissions. On Kosugi, I agree with you that the wording should centre on the general catalytic method and not on first discovery, which my citation does. I take your point that Hartwig's presence on another candidate is not a reason to reduce his credit here.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts C-N coupling as distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether the citation wording adequately handles Kosugi's and Migita's precursor chemistry in a two-person prize.
Whether B037 gains a regulatory approval or a settled attribution before the vote, which would change my assessment of its maturity.
Whether four B037 supporters can reach the five votes needed, or whether the vote will split and favour the consolidation candidate.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, who is a committee peer and not a candidate. My own field is electron crystallography and porous materials, and I have no mentorship, collaboration or institutional tie to any person credited on B005, B037 or B016 in the record I have.
